text:
josh: Quick Q — where can I see per-pool autoscale events (scale up/down) + the queue length that triggered them? Need to correlate for dedicated pool `eu-west-1-gpu-a`

tina: Grafana -> Observability -> Pools -> 'Autoscale Events by Pool'. Try: https://grafana.redwood/pools/autoscale?var-pool=eu-west-1-gpu-a. It shows events but no queue overlay by default.

raj: If you want queue-length overlay add this query to the panel: `sum(rate(dedicated_pool_inflight_requests_total{pool="eu-west-1-gpu-a"}[1m])) by (pool)` and use the right Y-axis. There's also `pool_steal_queue_length` for explicit queueing.

josh: Nice. Is there a prebuilt dashboard for saturation signals? Trying to tune the alert that fired last night.

kevin: :thumbsup: There's a 'Pool Saturation' dashboard. Alerts live in Alertmanager -> group 'eng-platform:pool-saturation'. Current alert expr: `avg_over_time(pool_utilization_ratio{job="pools"}[5m]) > 0.85` for 5m. That one can be noisy for known batch windows.

elaine: We bumped cooldown to 10m last month but left threshold. For load tests we sometimes add logic to suppress if `pending_scaledown` indicates scheduled ops. `unless on(pool) avg_over_time(pending_scaledown{pool!=""}[10m]) > 0` was used elsewhere — not perfect but reduces noise during planned work.

josh: Also noticed KV cache misses correlated with scale-ups. Where are KV cache metrics per-pool?

raj: KV cache panels live under Serving Runtime -> KVCache. Metric: `redwood_kvcache_hit_ratio{pool="eu-west-1-gpu-a"}`. Quick link: https://grafana.redwood/serving/kvcache.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: merged @raj 'add-pool-tag-to-autoscale-panel' (PR #4123) — dashboards updated.

tina: Quick ask — can someone change the alert severity to `warning` for this pool while we run a load test tomorrow? I'll file a pager-silence/exemption.

kevin: I can do that. Post start/end time and I'll update Alertmanager silence + temporarily lower severity.

josh: Load test window: 2026-03-22 09:00-11:00 UTC. I'll add context in #incidents in case it fires.

elaine: If you want end-to-end traces around the scale events use Tempo. You can add `X-Trace-Context` on test requests, or run: `redwoodctl traces query --pool eu-west-1-gpu-a --from 2026-03-22T08:50Z --to 2026-03-22T11:10Z` to capture the window.

josh: Great, thanks. I'll paste the grafana panels into the PR and ping when the silence is created. Anyone with tips for smoothing false positives (long tail spikes vs sustained saturation) share here.
